purpose: Screen every species -> compound link that yields a ChEMBL item under the verified-pilot-3.1 primary rule. The Tukey commonness fence counts curated Wikidata P703 taxa, so it measures how much literature is curated, not how common a compound is, and the approved-drug rule catches only max_phase 4. This review closes those gaps with the rejection classes the original-paper links already used.
rule: A link is rejected only on positive evidence of one class below, read from the cited paper's title or abstract (Crossref, Europe PMC) and the PubChem record of the stored InChIKey; otherwise it is accepted. Each entry holds the link's DOI set. The builder refuses a reviewed link whose DOIs differ (a new snapshot needs a new review) and a primary ChEMBL item whose link has no accepted entry.
scope: All 32 (species, InChIKey) links behind the 36 primary ChEMBL items of 2026-09-30, plus one original-paper link of the same class as a rejected link. Links that yield an item only in a rule_sensitivity view were not reviewed; the rejections below apply there as well.

classes.structure_mismatch: The stored structure is not the compound the paper reports (name collision, for example a carotenoid resolved to a purine).
classes.contaminant: Industrial chemical, pollutant, or product of an environmental element taken up by the organism, without evidence of natural origin in the paper.
classes.not_tissue: Reported from feces, gut contents or associated organisms, not the species' own tissue.
classes.ubiquitous_metabolite: Formed in essentially all organisms: C1 metabolites, amines from protein amino acids, common C16-C22 fatty acids and their C6-C10 oxidation aldehydes.

Isolated from the edible parts of C. sikamea from Zhanjiang, China (Kong et al. 2021, full text). None of the four rejection classes applies. Caveats for the page: flazin is also a known soy-sauce and fermentation beta-carboline, and the paper reports no spectra for its own isolate. Its ChEMBL anti-HIV rows come from two reviews and one synthesis paper that restate one earlier measurement (EC50 2.36 uM, Tang et al. 2008), so the activity side counts as one document.

Isolated from Korean 'Gelidium amansii' (Jeju) and identified by NMR and HR-MS (Park, Kim & Han 2022, full text); counted for G. elegans under the 2026-10-04 name-mapping decision. None of the four rejection classes applies. Caveats for the page: pheophorbide a is a chlorophyll breakdown product that also forms in harvested or dried algae, and the paper extracted dried thalli, so it may be a processing product rather than a compound of the living alga. The ChEMBL activity used (HIV-1, IC50) was measured on pheophorbide a from another source (Vatica cinerea; Zhang et al. 2003), as the stratum rule allows. A second paper by the same group (Kim, Kim & Han 2019, Phytother Res, doi:10.1002/ptr.6260) reports the compound from G. amansii but its full text was not reachable here, so it is not counted as a second link.
